messages:
Elaine Chen: Heads up — we started seeing a ~3x spike in 5xx for hosted inference at ~1739999960 right after the deploy. Affected routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. :rotating_light:
Samir Patel: I see the same in dashboards. Error rate jump from 0.4% -> 6.8% on prod. Latency also increased, tail P95 -> P99. Any recent flag flips?
Priya Kapoor: We rolled out the routing-weight-change config (routes.weight.v2) to 10% canary 20m ago. No other infra changes.
Alex Gomez: Oncall: can you snapshot a gateway log? I'm seeing a lot of gateway 502s with internal upstream timeouts.
sre-oncall-bot: Collected logs: /var/log/gateway/2026-03-17/1739999-gateway.log uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/incidents/1739999999/
Elaine Chen: Quick repro I ran locally against staging-like dataset: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response example: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream timeout","code":502}
```
Samir Patel: Looking at the gateway logs: most 502s include this snippet from the inference host: 
```
runtime: serve loop: kvcache.Get failed: context deadline exceeded
model: gpt-medium-8q -> handler: spawn timeout
```
Priya Kapoor: Hmm the routing-weight-change also toggles a batching-policy flag (batching.window=200ms -> 50ms) in the same config bundle. That could change kernel selection and cause higher CPU stalls for small sequences.
Alex Gomez: That lines up with CPU contention on the canary pool. I see increased preemption and a lot of batch flushes. Kernel watchdog kicking in, resulting in timeouts upstream.
Customer Support: We have 3 customers who just opened high-severity tickets — APIs failed for 2–3 minutes and then recovered. They reported "500 internal server error" and session disconnects.
Elaine Chen: Priority: pause canary routing and scale down affected pool. @Samir can you flip the routes.weight.v2 back to 0%?
Samir Patel: Initiating rollback now via orch: 
```
orch rollout set weights routes.weight.v2=0 --env=prod --reason="5xx spike canary rollback"
```
DeployBot: Rollout change accepted. Targeting orch controller nodes.
Samir Patel: Done — weights set to 0. Confirming traffic drain.
Alex Gomez: I'm attaching a minimal tracer from the problematic host: 
```
[tracer] 1739999 host=gpu-a12 zone=us-west2 batch=32 latency=462ms tokens=64 error=upstream-timeout
[trace] kernel=flash-attn2 queue_wait=120ms exec=310ms
```
Priya Kapoor: We should revert batching.window to previous setting for that model while we investigate. I'm opening a config rollback PR.
Elaine Chen: Ops helm patch applied to scale the canary pool down by 50% and spike protection enabled.
Customer Support: Notifying affected customers: sent apologies and ETA for root cause.
Samir Patel: Post-rollback metrics: error rate trending back down to baseline over 4m. P95 recovered.
Elaine Chen: Next steps: 1) block merging that config bundle until we run model-level perf tests, 2) add a rollout safety check that prevents batching.window reduction >50% without perf gates, 3) run offline perf runs on gpt-medium-8q with the 50ms window.
Alex Gomez: I will capture a repro job that simulates small-seq workloads with the new batching policy and attach perf traces.
Priya Kapoor: Filing follow-up ticket INF-7889 for rollout-safety gating + retain previous batching setting as default for canaries.
Elaine Chen: Thank you all — marking incident as mitigated but keeping thread open until postmortem. :white_check_mark:
